## 34f8510e39d0

**No issue found in the bounded audit.** Generator SHA-256
`da8ec3f3ac5ff927b23a00dffe466068134f99e73851d7581ed25f5a14c53bfa`;
selected rule hash `f97715331ac1`.

I generated samples 0–2 for seeds 0–199 in each of easy, medium and hard: 600
complete lessons and 1,800 inputs. All inputs passed `self_check` and
`strict_canonical_like`; every three-example lesson refuted all four declared
competitors (`fill_all_green`, `outline_all_nonzero_rectangles`,
`largest_green_only`, and `ignore_thin_green`). The scan covered every profile
used by the three difficulty schedules, with the thin-target witness in 200
inputs per band, multiple targets in 400 per band, and interior/distractor
witnesses in all 600 per band. It found 1,200 unique input hashes because some
profile schedules intentionally coincide across bands.

I also selected one ordinary generated input from each of the five exact scene
profiles and compared the task’s Python mirror with the supported canonical
Racket execution; all 5/5 matched. Evidence is
`checks/audit/34f8510e39d0/scan.json`, `representative_inputs.json`,
`racket.json`, and `authority_parity.json`.

This is not a universal proof. The generator intentionally restricts green
targets to isolated solid rectangles and the audit evaluated the declared
rivals plus ordinary generated profiles; an undeclared hypothesis or input
outside that documented grammar may behave differently. No audit-target source
was changed.
